reviewNote: Drafted by Claude from the chart for faculty review. Not validated teaching content.
summary: Elective carpal tunnel release under a Bier block in an HbSS patient three weeks after a vaso-occlusive crisis. Hematology advised against IV regional and tourniquet, she is alloimmunized (anti-E, anti-K) with no compatible blood for 24 to 48 h, there is no IV yet, and preop hydration has not started.

asa.rationale: HbSS with frequent crises, two episodes of acute chest syndrome, alloimmunization, chronic opioid therapy.

decision.rationale: Elective case, hematology suggests waiting 4 to 6 weeks after a crisis, and no compatible blood exists today. If done today: no Bier block; use a brachial plexus block or wide awake local anesthetic without tourniquet, with hydration, warming, oxygen. Otherwise delay and have blood bank prepare phenotype matched units.

redFlags.finding: IV regional anesthesia with tourniquet in HbSS
redFlags.evidence: Hematology 10/21: avoid tourniquet or IVRA if possible; surgeon kept Bier plan.
redFlags.implication: Venous stasis, acidosis and hypoxemia promote sickling, crisis, acute chest.
redFlags.action: Brachial plexus block or WALANT without tourniquet; if tourniquet unavoidable, short time, full exsanguination, oxygen, normothermia.

redFlags.evidence: Antibody screen positive, anti-E and anti-K; phenotype matched units need 24 to 48 h; blood bank not notified ahead; blood consent not signed.
redFlags.implication: No transfusion option if crisis or conversion to GA.
redFlags.action: Notify blood bank now; reconsider timing.

redFlags.implication: Higher risk of perioperative crisis and acute chest.
redFlags.action: Consider delay 4 to 6 weeks for an elective case.

redFlags.evidence: Two failed IV attempts; LR at 1.5x maintenance not started; cool extremities.
redFlags.action: Ultrasound guided IV, start fluids, forced air warming, oxygen to SpO2 95%.

redFlags.evidence: Oxycodone ER 15 q12h plus IR 10 mg 3 to 4 daily; taken 0500; morphine hives; NSAIDs avoided.
redFlags.action: Continue baseline opioids, regional anesthesia, multimodal non NSAID analgesia, hydromorphone for breakthrough.

planItems.item: Brachial plexus block or WALANT; avoid Bier block
Hydration, warming, oxygen SpO2 95% or higher
Cefazolin 2 g within 60 min of incision

boothComplications.why: Bier block or brachial plexus block
